verdict.rationale: NVIDIA publishes 141GB of HBM3e at 4.8 TB/s for the H200, enough to hold a 70B-class model on one GPU, and cites Llama2 70B inference running 1.9X faster than H100. Community comments agree that generative AI is memory-bound and that the faster, larger memory is the key upgrade. Missing for 10: explicit documentation or benchmarks for quantized 70B models, and independent hands-on single-GPU 70B inference results.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run a 70B-class quantized LLM on this GPU — published VRAM capacity and memory bandwidth that make local or single-node inference practical

citations.quote: the NVIDIA H200 is the first GPU to offer 141 gigabytes (GB) of HBM3e memory at 4.8 terabytes per second (TB/s)
the H200's larger and faster memory fuels the acceleration of generative AI and large language models (LLMs)
